**Summary**

On November 14, 2026, at 09:02:11, the account was accessed from a new device (DATO1) for the first time, followed by a password reset via email link at 09:04:40. Between 09:10:14 and 09:44:02, six P2P transactions totaling $9,800 were sent to three newly added payees (A060001, A060004, and A060007), with individual amounts ranging from $1,250 to $1,900—dramatically higher than the account's prior transaction history showing amounts under $300.

**Signals**

- **NEW_DEVICE**: First login from device DATO1 at 09:02:11, never used on this account before
- **RECENT_PASSWORD_RESET**: Password reset via email link at 09:04:40, just minutes before suspicious activity
- **FIRST_TIME_PAYEE**: Three new payees (A060001, A060004, A060007) added between 09:07:05 and 09:08:30, immediately before transactions
- **AMOUNT_SPIKE**: Six transactions of $1,250-$1,900 versus baseline activity of $6.82-$266.18 in preceding days
- **Linked accounts**: Link graph shows 9 connected accounts including all three recipient accounts (A060001, A060004, A060007), suggesting organized fraud ring

**Recommended next step**

Immediately block the account and all cards to prevent further unauthorized P2P transfers, and contact the legitimate account holder via verified phone number to confirm account takeover. Escalate the three recipient accounts (A060001, A060004, A060007) and all linked accounts in the fraud ring for investigation and potential blocking.

answers.text:
Only one merchant showed card-testing this week (Nov 8–14): **Zentrova Digital Goods**, which is in the Digital goods category.

- **396 card-testing alerts**, and each one was on a different card (396 cards)
- **$478.52 in total**, which works out to about $1.21 per authorization. That fits the rule, which flags many tiny card-not-present charges at one merchant within an hour.
- **All 396 alerts are labeled Fraud**, meaning a chargeback or issuer confirmation exists for each.

No other merchant set off the card-testing rule during the week.

answers.question: How many open high-priority alerts are there by channel?
answers.text:
There are 784 open high-priority alerts. Most of them (615, or about 78%) are card-not-present. P2P has 91 and card-present has 78.

| CHANNEL | OPEN_HIGH_ALERTS |
| --- | --- |
| CARD_NOT_PRESENT | 615 |
| P2P | 91 |
| CARD_PRESENT | 78 |

These counts cover every alert in the data set, raised from 2026-11-01 to 2026-11-14.

answers.question: Which merchant had the most false-positive alerts, and on which day?
answers.text:
**Quillmont Outfitters had the most false-positive alerts: 434 on November 8, 2026.** No other merchant had more than 4 in a single day, so this spike stands far above everything else.

| MERCHANT | ALERT_DATE | FP_ALERTS |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Quillmont Outfitters | 2026-11-08 | 434 |
| Harrowby Digital Online | 2026-11-09 | 4 |
| Istrel Bistro | 2026-11-02 | 4 |
| Kestrin Travel Online | 2026-11-05 | 4 |
| Pellmont Travel Online | 2026-11-11 | 3 |

All 434 alerts were card-not-present payments, and each came from a different account. 424 of them (about $67K) were flagged only for **NEW_DEVICE**. The card-testing rule didn't fire on any of them. This looks like one event that caused many customers to show up on new devices at the same time, such as an app or site change at the merchant, and not like fraud.

I counted alerts with the status FALSE_POSITIVE. Alerts labelled "Not fraud" that are still open aren't included.
